findings.failure_path: A later unreviewed fix can remove this step or replace its command while retaining the required job name. The job then succeeds without executing the binding gate, so including .github in the candidate hash does not prevent unreviewed content from merging.
findings.smallest_fix: Require a dedicated check produced by an immutable, externally controlled workflow or GitHub App/ruleset that PR contents cannot remove or redefine.

findings.failure_path: The gate accepts any committed JSON whose candidate hash matches and whose caller-controlled validator exits zero. Controller receipts are unsigned and the validator only checks their internal structure and hashes, so a contributor can fabricate a self-consistent ledger for the printed candidate without any external review and pass the merge gate.
findings.smallest_fix: Require receipts carrying an authenticity proof from a trusted controller outside the candidate tree, and verify that signature or attestation plus the candidate and chain bindings before invoking the structural ledger validator.

concern_results.conclusion: Two credible bypasses remain: the candidate can remove or neutralize its own CI enforcement step, and caller-authored unsigned receipts can be assembled into validator-accepted evidence without an external review.

Containment is not established because both the enforcement code and the evidence authenticity decision remain inside contributor-controlled repository state; the supplied tests verify ordinary behavior but cannot kill either trust-boundary bypass.
